items.title: G20 Rio de Janeiro Summit (Brazil 2024): Global Alliance Against Hunger and Poverty Launched
items.summary: The 19th G20 Summit convened in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, under President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, officially launching the 'Global Alliance Against Hunger and Poverty' and advancing the global governance reforms initiated during India's 2023 G20 Presidency.
items.crux: The summit focused on three core pillars: Social inclusion and the fight against hunger, energy transition and sustainable development, and reform of global governance institutions (UNSC, WTO, IMF).
takeaways: India, Brazil, and South Africa formed the G20 Troika, maintaining continuity on Global South priorities.
African Union (AU), inducted as a permanent member under India's G20 Presidency at New Delhi, participated in full capacity.
Endorsed progressive taxation on ultra-high-net-worth individuals and capital replenishment for Multilateral Development Banks (MDBs).

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: G20 2024 Presidency: Brazil; 2025 Presidency: South Africa. Theme: 'Building a Just World and a Sustainable Planet'.

options: Global Clean Hydrogen Compact

Global Artificial Intelligence Governance Treaty
mcq.explanation: The flagship deliverable of Brazil's G20 presidency was the Global Alliance Against Hunger and Poverty, endorsed by over 80 countries.

items.title: 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan, Russia: Historic Expansion Welcomes 5 New Member States
items.summary: The 16th BRICS Summit convened in Kazan, Russia, under the theme 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security', marking the first summit meeting since the formal expansion of BRICS to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates.
items.crux: Leaders adopted the comprehensive Kazan Declaration, reaffirming commitment to cross-border settlement in local currencies (BRICS Pay / BRICS Bridge) and reform of the Bretton Woods financial institutions and the UN Security Council.
takeaways: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping held their first formal bilateral meeting in five years on the sidelines of the summit following the patrolling pact along the Line of Actual Control (LAC).
BRICS represents over 45% of the world's population and roughly 35% of global GDP by Purchasing Power Parity (PPP).
Created a new category of 'BRICS Partner Countries' to engage non-member developing economies.

options: Rakesh Kumar
Sheetal Devi
Harvinder Singh
Vivek Chikara
mcq.explanation: Harvinder Singh made history by defeating Poland's Lukasz Ciszek to win India's first-ever Paralympic Gold in Archery.

items.title: Exercise Tarang Shakti 2024: India's Largest-Ever Multilateral Air Force Combat Drill
items.summary: The Indian Air Force (IAF) conducted 'Exercise Tarang Shakti 2024', the largest multilateral air combat exercise ever hosted on Indian soil, involving air forces and observers from over 30 countries across two phases in Sulur (Tamil Nadu) and Jodhpur (Rajasthan).
items.crux: Showcased complex composite air operations and interoperability between Western and Eastern fighter jets, featuring Eurofighter Typhoons, Rafales, F-15s, Su-30MKIs, Tejas LCAs, and aerial refuelers.
takeaways: Participating nations included Australia, France, Germany, Spain, the United Kingdom, the United States, Japan, and the UAE.
Phase 1 held at Sulur Air Force Station; Phase 2 held at Jodhpur Air Force Station.
Demonstrated the operational prowess of indigenous aviation platforms including the LCA Tejas, Prachand LCH, and Netra AEW&C.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: First edition of India's largest multinational air exercise; Over 150 aircraft from 10+ participating nations and 18 observer nations.

mcq.question: What was the name of the largest-ever multilateral air combat exercise hosted on Indian soil by the Indian Air Force?
options: Exercise Desert Knight
Exercise Tarang Shakti
Exercise Garuda
Exercise Pitch Black
mcq.explanation: Exercise Tarang Shakti 2024 was the largest multilateral air combat drill hosted by the IAF, with two phases held in Sulur and Jodhpur.

items.title: INS Arighaat: Second Indigenous Nuclear Ballistic Missile Submarine (SSBN) Commissioned
items.summary: India commissioned its second indigenous nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine, INS Arighaat (S3), into the Indian Navy at Visakhapatnam in the presence of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh.
items.crux: INS Arighaat cements India's assured second-strike capability and solidifies the sea-based leg of the nuclear triad under the Advanced Technology Vessel (ATV) project.
takeaways: Built with indigenous DMR 249A high-tensile steel, powered by an 83 MW pressurized light-water reactor (PWR) using enriched uranium.
Armed with indigenous K-15 Sagarika submarine-launched ballistic missiles (SLBM, 750 km range) and capable of carrying K-4 missiles (3,500 km range).
Follows lead vessel INS Arihant (commissioned in 2016); third submarine INS Aridhaman is under sea trials.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Commissioned: August 29, 2024. Reactor: 83 MW PWR. Missiles: K-15 (750 km) & K-4 (3,500 km).

mcq.question: What is the primary strategic role of INS Arighaat in India's national security doctrine?
options: Anti-piracy patrols in the Strait of Malacca.
Sea-based second-strike nuclear deterrence as part of the nuclear triad.
Amphibious troop landing in island territories.
Aircraft carrier battle group escort vessel.
mcq.explanation: INS Arighaat is a Ship Submersible Ballistic Nuclear (SSBN) vessel designed for continuous at-sea deterrence, providing credible second-strike capability.

items.title: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) Completes 10 Years: Crosses 53 Crore Accounts
items.summary: The National Mission for Financial Inclusion, PMJDY, marked a decade since its launch in August 2014, surpassing 53.1 crore bank accounts with cumulative deposits exceeding ₹2.31 lakh crore.
items.crux: Over 67% of PMJDY accounts are located in rural and semi-urban branches, and 55.6% of accounts belong to women beneficiaries, underpinning the JAM (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile) trinity.
takeaways: Provides zero balance Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account (BSBDA) with free RuPay debit card and ₹2 lakh accidental insurance cover.
Offers an overdraft (OD) facility up to ₹10,000 for eligible account holders with no conditions up to ₹2,000.
Operates as the primary pipeline for Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) across central welfare schemes like PM-KISAN, PM-GKY, and LPG subsidies.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Total accounts: 53+ Cr; RuPay cards issued: 36+ Cr; Zero-balance accounts dropped from 58% in 2015 to under 8% in 2024.

mcq.question: What is the maximum Overdraft (OD) facility limit available to an eligible PMJDY account holder?
mcq.explanation: The overdraft limit under PMJDY was enhanced from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000 with no conditions for overdraft up to ₹2,000.

items.title: UPI Global Expansion: Cross-Border Linkages with UAE, France, Singapore, Mauritius & Sri Lanka
items.summary: NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL) expanded the footprint of the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) to international destinations including UAE (AANI/Jaywan), France, Mauritius, Sri Lanka, and Singapore.
items.crux: Indian travelers can scan local QR codes to make real-time rupee payments abroad without foreign exchange markups, boosting the internationalization of the Indian Rupee.
takeaways: France became the first European country to accept UPI, starting with ticket bookings at the iconic Eiffel Tower.
UPI-PayNow linkage between India and Singapore enables real-time cross-border P2P remittances.
NIPL signed agreement with UAE's Al Etihad Payments to roll out domestic card scheme Jaywan based on RuPay tech.

prelims_pointers.location: Global / Paris / Abu Dhabi / Singapore / Colombo
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: NPCI was created by RBI and Indian Banks' Association (IBA) as a not-for-profit company under Section 8 of Companies Act 2013.

mcq.question: Which was the first European country to operationalize Unified Payments Interface (UPI) payments for tourists?
options: Germany
United Kingdom
France
Switzerland
mcq.explanation: France became the first European country to launch UPI, enabling tourists to purchase tickets at the Eiffel Tower using UPI apps.

items.title: India Adds 3 New Ramsar Sites: Total Network Reaches 85 Wetlands of International Importance
items.summary: On the eve of Independence Day 2024, India designated three more wetlands as Ramsar sites of international importance: Nanjarayan Bird Sanctuary and Kazhuveli Bird Sanctuary in Tamil Nadu, and Tawa Reservoir in Madhya Pradesh, expanding the national network to 85 Ramsar sites.
items.crux: India holds the largest network of Ramsar sites in South Asia and the third largest globally, protecting over 1.35 million hectares of fragile freshwater and coastal ecosystems.
takeaways: Tamil Nadu holds the highest number of Ramsar sites in India (18 sites), followed by Uttar Pradesh (10 sites).
Nanjarayan Bird Sanctuary is an ancient large waterbody in Tiruppur district supporting bar-headed geese and migratory birds.
Kazhuveli Bird Sanctuary on the Coromandel coast is one of the largest brackish water wetlands in peninsular India.
Tawa Reservoir, created by the dam on the Tawa River inside Satpura Tiger Reserve, forms a crucial haven for aquatic flora and wintering waterfowl.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Total Ramsar sites in India: 85 sites. State with most sites: Tamil Nadu (18). India ratified Ramsar convention on Feb 1, 1982.

mcq.question: Which Indian state currently possesses the highest number of designated Ramsar wetland sites in the country?
options: Uttar Pradesh
Tamil Nadu
Kerala
West Bengal
mcq.explanation: Tamil Nadu leads India with 18 designated Ramsar sites, followed by Uttar Pradesh with 10 sites.

items.title: Paris 2024 Olympic Games: Manu Bhaker Makes History with Double Bronze; Neeraj Wins Silver
items.summary: India concluded its campaign at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games with 6 medals (1 Silver, 5 Bronze), highlighted by shooter Manu Bhaker becoming the first Indian athlete in post-independence history to win two medals at a single Olympics.
items.crux: Manu Bhaker won Bronze in Women's 10m Air Pistol and Bronze in 10m Air Pistol Mixed Team with Sarabjot Singh. Neeraj Chopra won Silver in Men's Javelin with 89.45m. Indian Men's Hockey team bagged Bronze beating Spain 2-1.
takeaways: Aman Sehrawat won Bronze in Men's 57kg Freestyle Wrestling, becoming India's youngest individual Olympic medalist at age 21.
Swapnil Kusale won Bronze in Men's 50m Rifle 3 Positions (India's first-ever Olympic medal in this event).
PR Sreejesh retired from international hockey following India's heroic bronze victory against Spain.
Pakistan's Arshad Nadeem won Javelin Gold with an Olympic record throw of 92.97m.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Total medals: 6 (1 Silver, 5 Bronze); Manu Bhaker: first double medalist in single Games; Flagbearers at closing ceremony: Manu Bhaker & PR Sreejesh.

mcq.question: Who became the first athlete in post-independence Indian history to win two Olympic medals at a single edition of the Olympic Games?
options: Neeraj Chopra
Manu Bhaker
PV Sindhu
Sushil Kumar
mcq.explanation: Manu Bhaker made history at Paris 2024 by winning two bronze medals: one in the individual women's 10m air pistol and another in the mixed team event with Sarabjot Singh.

items.title: Supreme Court 7-Judge Bench Permits Sub-Classification of SCs and STs for Quota
items.summary: In a 6:1 landmark ruling in State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh, a 7-judge Constitution bench ruled that state governments have constitutional power to create sub-categories within Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes to ensure affirmative action reaches the most backward communities.
items.crux: The judgment overruled the 2004 E.V. Chinnaiah ruling, holding that sub-classification does not violate Article 341 or tinker with the Presidential list as long as it is backed by empirical data.
takeaways: States cannot reserve 100% of seats for any sub-group; sub-classification must be based on objective empirical evidence of inadequate representation.
Four out of seven judges opined that the 'creamy layer' principle should also apply to SCs and STs to exclude affluent members from reservations.
Affirmed that substantive equality under Article 14 requires differential treatment for unequals within a broadly designated caste group.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Case: State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh. Overruled E.V. Chinnaiah (2004). Bench headed by CJI D.Y. Chandrachud (6:1 majority; Justice Bela Trivedi dissented).

mcq.question: Which earlier landmark judgment was overruled by the 7-judge bench of the Supreme Court in the 2024 SC/ST sub-classification verdict?
options: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992)
E.V. Chinnaiah v. State of Andhra Pradesh (2004)
M. Nagaraj v. Union of India (2006)
Jarnail Singh v. Lachhmi Narain Gupta (2018)
mcq.explanation: The 2024 bench overruled the 2004 five-judge bench decision in E.V. Chinnaiah, which had held that the Presidential list of SCs under Article 341 formed a single homogeneous class that could not be sub-divided.

items.title: Moidams of Ahom Dynasty in Assam Inscribed as India's 43rd UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.summary: At the 46th session of the World Heritage Committee in New Delhi, the Charaideo Moidams (mound-burial system of the Ahom Dynasty) were inscribed onto the UNESCO World Heritage List, becoming the first cultural site from Northeast India to gain this status.
items.crux: Known as the 'Pyramids of Assam', the Moidams represent the 600-year-old royal burial tradition and tai-ahom funerary architecture situated in Charaideo, the first capital of the Ahom kingdom founded by Chao Lung Siu-Ka-Pha in 1253 AD.
takeaways: India now has 43 UNESCO World Heritage Sites (35 cultural, 7 natural, 1 mixed - Khangchendzonga).
Moidams feature a vaulted chamber (Chaw-Chali), earth mounds covered by grass, and octagonal boundary walls with a shrine on top (Chow-chali).
First World Heritage Committee session hosted by India took place in New Delhi in July 2024.

prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: 43rd UNESCO World Heritage site in India; 1st cultural site from Northeast India; Built by Ahom kings (13th-18th century).

mcq.question: The Charaideo Moidams, recently inscribed as India's 43rd UNESCO World Heritage Site, belong to which historic ruling dynasty?
options: Pala Dynasty
Koch Dynasty
Ahom Dynasty
Kamata Dynasty
mcq.explanation: Moidams are the sacred royal burial mounds of the Ahom kings and queens in Charaideo, Assam, who ruled the Brahmaputra valley for over 600 years.

items.title: SEBI Launches T+0 Same-Day Rolling Settlement Cycle on Optional Basis
items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) introduced a beta version of the T+0 settlement cycle for equity cash segments on an optional basis for select liquid stocks.
items.crux: Under T+0 settlement, sellers receive cash and buyers receive shares in their demat accounts on the same day of the trade transaction.
takeaways: India became the second country after China to implement T+1 settlement in 2023, and is now pioneering T+0 same-day settlement.
Enhances market liquidity, reduces settlement risk, and lowers capital margin requirements for institutional and retail traders.
SEBI plans eventual transition toward instantaneous (T+instant) settlement using blockchain/distributed ledger technology.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: SEBI was established as a statutory body in 1992 following the SEBI Act. Current Chairperson: Madhabi Puri Buch.

mcq.question: In financial markets terminology, what does the implementation of 'T+0' settlement signify?
options: Settlement of trades strictly at zero brokerage fees.
Transfer of funds and securities on the very day the trade is executed.
Settlement within zero business hours before market opens.
Mandatory 24-hour cooling-off period before shares can be traded.
mcq.explanation: T+0 implies same-day settlement: the shares and funds are exchanged between buyer and seller on the same trading day (Day 0).

items.title: Three New Criminal Laws (BNS, BNSS, BSA) Come into Force Across India
items.summary: Three historic criminal laws came into full effect on July 1, 2024: the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) replacing the Indian Penal Code 1860, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) replacing the CrPC 1973, and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) replacing the Indian Evidence Act 1872.
items.crux: The new laws modernize India's criminal justice system by digitizing forensics, introducing Zero FIR, e-FIR, community service as punishment, and replacing the archaic sedition law with acts endangering sovereignty.
takeaways: BNS replaces sedition (IPC Section 124A) with Section 152 penalizing acts endangering the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
BNSS makes forensic examination mandatory for offenses punishable by 7 years of imprisonment or more.
Introduces community service as a penal sentence for minor offenses (first time in Indian criminal law).
BSA grants legal admissibility to electronic and digital records as primary evidence on par with physical documents.

prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: BNS Act 2023, BNSS Act 2023, BSA Act 2023
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Date of enforcement: July 1, 2024. Replaced colonial laws dating back to 1860, 1872, and 1973.

mcq.question: Under the newly enacted Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, forensic investigation by scientific experts is made mandatory for offenses punishable with imprisonment of:
options: 3 years or more
5 years or more
7 years or more
10 years or more
mcq.explanation: BNSS mandates forensic inspection at the scene of crime for all offenses punishable with imprisonment of seven years or more.

items.title: ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024: India Crowned World Champions Defeating South Africa
items.summary: India ended an 11-year ICC trophy drought by winning the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024, defeating South Africa by 7 runs in a nail-biting final at Kensington Oval in Bridgetown, Barbados.
items.crux: India became the first team to win the Men's T20 World Cup undefeated throughout the tournament. Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli announced their retirement from T20 International cricket following the victory.
takeaways: Virat Kohli was named Player of the Match in the final for his match-winning 76 off 59 balls.
Jasprit Bumrah was adjudged Player of the Tournament, taking 15 wickets at an astonishing economy rate of 4.17.
Suryakumar Yadav took a legendary boundary catch on the first ball of the final over off Hardik Pandya to dismiss David Miller.
Rahul Dravid concluded his tenure as Head Coach of the Indian Men's Cricket Team on a triumphant note.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) & ICC
prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: 9th ICC Men's T20 World Cup (Co-hosted by USA & West Indies)
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: India's 2nd T20 World Cup title (after 2007); Undefeated champions; Final margin: 7 runs; Player of Tournament: Jasprit Bumrah.

mcq.question: Who was adjudged the Player of the Tournament at the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024?
options: Virat Kohli
Jasprit Bumrah
Rohit Sharma
Hardik Pandya
mcq.explanation: Jasprit Bumrah was named Player of the Tournament for taking 15 wickets at an average of 8.26 and a tournament-best economy rate of 4.17.

items.title: Critical Minerals Mission: First Tranche of Offshore & Onshore Critical Mineral Blocks Auctioned
items.summary: The Ministry of Mines successfully completed the auction of critical mineral blocks including Lithium, Rare Earth Elements (REE), Titanium, Graphite, and Nickel across Jammu & Kashmir, Chhattisgarh, and offshore exclusive economic zones.
items.crux: Secures essential supply chains for electric vehicles (EV), renewable batteries, solar photovoltaic panels, and defence aerospace, reducing import dependency on China.
takeaways: Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act 2023 removed 6 atomic minerals (including Lithium and Beryllium) from the atomic list, opening them to private commercial mining.
Offshore Areas Mineral (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act enables transparent auction of seabed mineral reserves in India's EEZ.
KABIL (Khanij Bidesh India Ltd), a JV of NALCO, HCL, and MECL, acquired 5 lithium brine blocks in Catamarca province, Argentina.

prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: MMDR Amendment Act 2023 & Offshore Areas Mineral Act 2023
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: India identified 30 critical minerals essential for economic development and national security.

mcq.question: Khanij Bidesh India Limited (KABIL) has secured lithium exploration and mining rights in which South American nation?
options: Bolivia
Chile
Argentina
Brazil
mcq.explanation: KABIL signed an agreement with the state-owned CAMYEN in Catamarca province, Argentina, to explore and develop 5 lithium brine blocks.

items.title: PM Vishwakarma Scheme: Financial Aid & Skill Toolkits for 18 Traditional Artisan Trades
items.summary: The Central Sector Scheme 'PM Vishwakarma' marked over 2 crore applications across India, providing collateral-free credit, enterprise skill training, and modern toolkit incentives to uplift traditional craftspeople and artisans.
items.crux: Covers 18 traditional trades (carpenters, blacksmiths, goldsmiths, potters, sculptors, cobblers, weavers) with collateral-free enterprise loans up to ₹3 lakh at a concessional 5% interest rate.
takeaways: Beneficiaries receive ₹500/day stipend during basic skill training and a ₹15,000 digital e-voucher for purchasing modern toolkits.
Provides PM Vishwakarma Certificate and ID card, brand building, and linkage with e-commerce platforms like GeM and ONDC.
Funded entirely by the Central Government with an outlay of ₹13,000 crore for a period of five years (FY24 to FY28).

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Ministry of MSME, Ministry of Skill Development, Ministry of Finance
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: 18 traditional trades covered. Concessional loan: ₹1 lakh (Tranche 1) + ₹2 lakh (Tranche 2) at 5% interest. Toolkit incentive: ₹15,000.

mcq.question: How many traditional crafts and trades are eligible for financial support under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme?
options: 12 trades
15 trades
18 trades
24 trades
mcq.explanation: The PM Vishwakarma scheme covers 18 traditional artisanal trades spanning wood, iron, clay, stone, and leather craftsmanship.

items.title: High-Level Committee on Simultaneous Elections (One Nation, One Election) Submits Report
items.summary: The High-Level Committee on Simultaneous Elections headed by former President Ram Nath Kovind presented its comprehensive report to the President of India, recommending synchronized elections for Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.
items.crux: Recommends a two-step implementation: synchronizing Lok Sabha and Assembly elections in Step 1, followed by synchronizing municipal and panchayat elections within 100 days in Step 2.
takeaways: Proposes amendment to Article 82A introducing an 'Appointed Date' to harmonize state legislative assembly terms with Lok Sabha.
Recommended introducing a Single Electoral Roll and Single Elector's Photo Identity Card (EPIC) across all three tiers of government.
In the event of a hung assembly or no-confidence motion, fresh elections would be held only for the 'unexpired term' of the House.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Chairman: Ram Nath Kovind; Members included Amit Shah, Ghulam Nabi Azad, N.K. Singh, Subhash Kashyap, Harish Salve, Sanjay Kothari.

mcq.question: The Kovind Committee on Simultaneous Elections recommended that in the event of a mid-term dissolution of a state assembly, the newly elected assembly should serve for:
options: A fresh full term of 5 years.
Only the unexpired remainder of the original term.
A fixed probationary period of 2.5 years.
Until the President dissolves it under Article 356.
mcq.explanation: To maintain synchronization, the committee recommended that mid-term elected assemblies will continue only for the unexpired term until the next general election.

items.source: PIB / Ministry of Law and Justice

items.title: India Signs Historic TEPA Free Trade Agreement with EFTA: $100 Billion Investment Commitment
items.summary: India and the 4-nation European Free Trade Association (EFTA: Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, and Liechtenstein) signed the Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA), featuring a legally binding commitment to invest $100 billion in India over 15 years.
items.crux: TEPA marks India's first FTA with a European bloc featuring binding foreign direct investment obligations, generating an estimated 1 million direct jobs in manufacturing and green tech.
takeaways: EFTA is a non-EU trade bloc established in 1960 promoting free trade among members.
Eliminates tariffs on 99.6% of India's exports to EFTA nations including gems, jewelry, textiles, machinery, and pharma.
Excludes sensitive sectors like dairy, soya, and gold from zero-duty concessions to protect domestic producers.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: EFTA members: Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein. Investment pledge: $100 billion over 15 years; 1 million jobs.

mcq.question: Which of the following nations is NOT a member of the European Free Trade Association (EFTA)?
options: Switzerland
Norway
Sweden
Iceland
mcq.explanation: Sweden is a member of the European Union (EU), not EFTA. EFTA consists of 4 non-EU nations: Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, and Liechtenstein.

items.title: IndiaAI Mission Approved with ₹10,372 Crore Outlay: 10,000+ GPU Supercomputing Capacity
items.summary: The Union Cabinet approved the comprehensive national-level IndiaAI Mission with a budget of ₹10,371.92 crore to democratize AI compute infrastructure, build indigenous foundational models, and foster startup innovation.
items.crux: Establishes a public-private AI compute capacity of 10,000 or more Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) made available to researchers and startups at subsidized rates.
takeaways: Components include: IndiaAI Compute Capacity, IndiaAI Innovation Centre (developing multi-modal indigenous LLMs), IndiaAI Datasets Platform, IndiaAI FutureSkills (data literacy programs).
Promotes AI applications in agriculture, healthcare, climate change, and vernacular language translation (Bhashini platform).
Sets up an IndiaAI Safe & Trusted AI framework to mitigate ethical bias and algorithmic risks.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Budget: ₹10,372 crore. Compute target: 10,000+ GPUs. Core pillars: Compute, Datasets, LLMs, Skills, Ethics.

mcq.question: Under the IndiaAI Mission approved by the Union Cabinet, what is the targeted supercomputing compute capacity planned for startups and researchers?
options: 1,000 GPUs
5,000 GPUs
10,000 or more GPUs
50,000 GPUs
mcq.explanation: The mission targets establishing an AI compute infrastructure comprising 10,000 or more Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) under public-private partnership.

items.title: India's First Commercial Semiconductor Fabrication Plant Approved in Dholera, Gujarat
items.summary: The Union Cabinet approved the establishment of India's first commercial semiconductor fabrication facility in Dholera Special Investment Region (SIR), Gujarat, by Tata Electronics in partnership with Taiwan's Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp (PSMC).
items.crux: With an investment of ₹91,000 crore, the fab will have a capacity of 50,000 wafer starts per month, producing 28nm, 40nm, 55nm, and 90nm chips for automotive, computing, and telecommunications.
takeaways: Part of the ₹76,000 crore ($10 billion) India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) launched under Digital India Corporation.
Two additional packaging units approved: Tata Semiconductor Assembly & Test (TSAT) in Morigaon, Assam (₹27,000 cr) and CG Power in Sanand, Gujarat.
Dholera SIR is India's first platinum-rated greenfield smart city developed along the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC).

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Fab partner: PSMC (Taiwan). Technology nodes: 28nm to 90nm. Total semiconductor projects outlay approved exceeds ₹1.25 lakh crore.

mcq.question: India's first commercial semiconductor wafer fabrication plant is being established at which location?
options: Sanand, Gujarat
Dholera, Gujarat
Morigaon, Assam
Sri City, Andhra Pradesh
mcq.explanation: Tata Electronics and Taiwan's PSMC are setting up India's first commercial fab plant at Dholera SIR in Gujarat.

items.title: International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) Headquarters Formally Established in India
items.summary: The Union Cabinet approved the establishment of the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) with headquarters in India, providing a one-time budgetary support of ₹150 crore for five years to spearhead conservation of the world's seven major big cat species.
items.crux: The alliance focuses on protecting the Tiger, Lion, Leopard, Snow Leopard, Cheetah, Jaguar, and Puma across 96 range countries, replicating the success of India's Project Tiger.
takeaways: India is the only country in the world that naturally hosts five of the seven big cats in the wild (Tiger, Lion, Leopard, Snow Leopard, and Cheetah).
IBCA framework mirrors the International Solar Alliance (ISA) model, establishing a treaty-based international organization.
India's wild tiger population stands at 3,682 (over 75% of global tiger population) as per the All India Tiger Estimation 2022.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: 7 big cats: Tiger, Lion, Leopard, Snow Leopard, Cheetah, Jaguar, Puma. India naturally hosts 5 of them.

mcq.question: Which of the following big cat species is NOT found naturally in the wild in India?
options: Snow Leopard
Asiatic Lion
Jaguar
Leopard
mcq.explanation: Jaguars are native to the Americas (Central and South America). India naturally hosts Tigers, Asiatic Lions, Leopards, Snow Leopards, and reintroduced Cheetahs.

items.title: Supreme Court Unanimously Strikes Down Electoral Bonds Scheme as Unconstitutional
items.summary: A 5-judge Constitution Bench headed by CJI D.Y. Chandrachud unanimously invalidated the 2018 Electoral Bonds Scheme, ruling that anonymous corporate political funding violates the voters' right to information under Article 19(1)(a).
items.crux: The Supreme Court struck down amendments to the Companies Act, Representation of the People Act, and Income Tax Act, ordering SBI to disclose all donor and recipient bond data to ECI for public display.
takeaways: Ruled that voter's right to information is essential to exercise freedom of speech and expression and to evaluate corporate influence on government policy.
Rejected the government's argument that confidentiality of political donors is necessary to curb black money (doctrine of proportionality failed).
Struck down amendment to Section 182 of Companies Act that had removed the 7.5% cap on corporate political donations.

prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Article 19(1)(a), Article 14, Representation of the People Act 1951
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Case title: Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR) v. Union of India. Unanimous 5-0 judgment.

mcq.question: In the landmark judgment invalidating the Electoral Bonds Scheme, the Supreme Court held that donor anonymity violates:
options: Right to Equality under Article 14 exclusively.
Voters' fundamental right to information under Article 19(1)(a).
Right to Privacy of corporate donors under Article 21.
Article 324 powers of the Election Commission.
mcq.explanation: The Court held that voters have a fundamental right to know about political funding sources under Article 19(1)(a) to prevent corrupt quid pro quo arrangements.

items.source: Supreme Court of India / The Hindu

items.title: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana Launched with ₹75,021 Crore Outlay for 1 Crore Rooftop Solar Systems
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the mega clean energy scheme 'PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana' providing direct capital subsidies to install rooftop solar panels for 1 crore households, delivering up to 300 units of free electricity every month.
items.crux: Households receive a central financial assistance (CFA) subsidy up to ₹78,000 for 3 kW solar plants, reducing household power bills and enabling families to earn income by selling surplus power to the discom grid.
takeaways: Subsidy structure: ₹30,000 for 1 kW systems, ₹60,000 for 2 kW systems, and ₹78,000 for 3 kW and higher capacity systems.
Supported by collateral-free low-interest bank loans (at 7% interest rate) via National Portal for Rooftop Solar.
Expected to add 30 GW of residential rooftop solar capacity, reducing 720 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent emissions over 25 years.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)

items.title: Vadnagar Excavations: Continuous Human Settlement for 2,800 Years Confirmed by ASI
items.summary: A deep multidisciplinary excavation at Vadnagar in Mehsana district, Gujarat, led by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) in collaboration with IIT Kharagpur, unearthed evidence of continuous human occupation dating back to 800 BCE.
items.crux: Challenges the notion of a 'Dark Age' between the decline of the Indus Valley Civilization and the Second Urbanization of the Gangetic Plains, proving unbroken cultural continuity through 7 distinct cultural periods.
takeaways: Seven cultural periods identified: Pre-Rampart (Mauryan/Pre-Mauryan), Indo-Greek, Indo-Scythian/Kshatrapa, Maitraka/Solanki, Sultanate, Mughal, and Gaekwad.
Uncovered Buddhist monastery ruins, amphitheater, Roman amphora pottery shards, and shell bangles proving trans-oceanic trade links.
Vadnagar was mentioned as 'Anartapura' in the Mahabharata and visited by Chinese traveler Hiuen Tsang in the 7th century CE.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) & IIT Kharagpur
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Chronology: 800 BCE to modern era (2,800 years); 7 cultural strata; Visited by Hiuen Tsang (640 CE) who described 10 Buddhist monasteries.

mcq.question: Which Chinese Buddhist pilgrim visited the ancient town of Vadnagar (then Anandapura) in the 7th century CE and recorded the existence of Buddhist monasteries?
options: Fa-Hien
Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang)
I-Tsing
Song Yun
mcq.explanation: Hiuen Tsang visited Vadnagar in 640 CE, writing that Anandapura was a major center with 10 Buddhist monasteries housing over 1,000 monks of the Sammitiya school.

items.title: 16th Finance Commission Formally Commences Work Under Dr. Arvind Panagariya
items.summary: The 16th Finance Commission, constituted under Article 280 of the Constitution and chaired by former NITI Aayog Vice Chairman Dr. Arvind Panagariya, began state consultations to determine vertical and horizontal tax devolution for 2026-2031.
items.crux: The Commission will recommend the sharing of net proceeds of taxes between Union and States, grants-in-aid to States, and measures to augment the consolidated funds of States to supplement panchayats and municipalities.
takeaways: Award period: 5 years commencing April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2031.
The 15th Finance Commission (chaired by N.K. Singh) had recommended 41% vertical devolution to States (retaining 1% for J&K and Ladakh).
Key terms of reference include reviewing financing of Disaster Management initiatives under the Disaster Management Act, 2005.

prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Article 280 & 281 of the Constitution of India
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Chairman: Dr. Arvind Panagariya; Secretary: Ritvik Ranjanam Pandey; Report submission deadline: October 31, 2025.

mcq.question: Under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution, the Finance Commission is constituted by:
options: The Prime Minister of India on recommendation of the Cabinet.
The President of India at the expiration of every fifth year or earlier.
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha in consultation with State Governors.
The Union Minister of Finance.
mcq.explanation: Article 280(1) mandates the President to constitute a Finance Commission within two years from commencement and thereafter at the expiration of every fifth year.

items.title: Rohan Bopanna Becomes Oldest Grand Slam Champion and World No. 1 in Tennis History
items.summary: At the age of 43 years and 329 days, Indian tennis veteran Rohan Bopanna became the oldest first-time World No. 1 and the oldest male Grand Slam champion in the Open Era by winning the 2024 Australian Open Men's Doubles title partnering Matthew Ebden.
items.crux: Bopanna and Ebden defeated the Italian duo of Simone Bolelli and Andrea Vavassori 7-6, 7-5 in the final at Rod Laver Arena in Melbourne.
takeaways: Bopanna broke the previous record held by Jean-Julien Rojer (40 years 9 months) to become the oldest major champion in men's doubles.
This marked Bopanna's first men's doubles Grand Slam title and second major overall (after his 2017 French Open Mixed Doubles title with Gabriela Dabrowski).
Bopanna was conferred with the Padma Shri, India's fourth highest civilian honor, in 2024.

items.title: Swachh Survekshan Awards: Indore and Surat Crowned Joint Cleanest Cities in India
items.summary: President Droupadi Murmu presented the Swachh Survekshan Awards, where Indore (for an unprecedented 7th straight year) and Surat were declared joint winners for the cleanest city in India in the category of cities with population over 1 lakh.
items.crux: Navi Mumbai was ranked the third cleanest city. Maharashtra bagged the top prize for the cleanest state in India, followed by Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.
takeaways: Sasvad in Maharashtra bagged the top award for cleanest city among small towns with population under 1 lakh.
Varanasi and Prayagraj were recognized as the cleanest Ganga towns.
Mhow Cantonment Board in Madhya Pradesh was judged the cleanest cantonment board in the country.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Cleanest City (>1 lakh): Indore & Surat (Joint 1st); Cleanest State: Maharashtra; Cleanest Ganga Town: Varanasi.

items.title: UNESCO Inscribes 'Garba of Gujarat' on Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage
items.summary: UNESCO officially inscribed 'Garba of Gujarat' onto the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity (ICH), making it the 15th intangible cultural heritage element from India on the list.
items.crux: Garba is a devotional ritualistic dance performed during the nine-day Hindu festival of Navratri, celebrating the divine feminine force (Shakti) symbolized by a perforated earthen pot (Garbha Deep) with an oil lamp inside.
takeaways: Celebrates social inclusivity, gender equality, and communal bonding across all sections of society.
Earlier Indian entries on UNESCO ICH list include Durga Puja in Kolkata (2021), Kumbh Mela (2017), Yoga (2016), and Vedic chanting (2008).
The decision was announced during the 18th session of the Intergovernmental Committee for the Safeguarding of the ICH held in Kasane, Botswana.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Ministry of Culture & Sangeet Natak Akademi
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: 15th Indian element on UNESCO ICH list; Performed during Sharad Navratri around Garbha Deep.

mcq.question: Which of the following elements is the 15th Intangible Cultural Heritage from India to be inscribed by UNESCO?
options: Chhau dance
Durga Puja of Kolkata
Garba of Gujarat
Kumbh Mela
mcq.explanation: Garba of Gujarat was inscribed as the 15th element from India on UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in December 2023.

items.title: Aditya-L1 Solar Mission Enters Halo Orbit at Lagrange Point 1 (L1)
items.summary: ISRO's maiden solar mission, Aditya-L1, successfully performed its final orbital injection burn to enter a five-year halo orbit around the Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 1 (L1), 1.5 million kilometers from Earth.
items.crux: From L1, Aditya-L1 enjoys an uninterrupted view of the Sun without eclipses or occultation, observing space weather, solar flares, and coronal mass ejections (CMEs).
takeaways: Carries 7 scientific payloads: 4 for direct remote sensing of the Sun (VELC, SUIT, ASPEX, PAPA) and 3 for in-situ solar wind measurements.
Lagrange points are equilibrium positions in space where gravitational pull of two large masses equals the centripetal force required to move with them.
Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC) designed by Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA) captures high-resolution coronal images.

prelims_pointers.location: Lagrange Point 1 (L1), 1.5 million km from Earth
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Launched aboard PSLV-C57 from Sriharikota on Sept 2, 2023; inserted into halo orbit Jan 6, 2024. Operates 7 payloads.

mcq.question: Why is the Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 1 (L1) chosen as the observation orbital location for the Aditya-L1 spacecraft?
options: It is located exactly halfway between Earth and Mars.
It allows continuous, unhindered observation of the Sun without occultation or eclipses.
It is completely shielded from solar wind and radiation.
It is the point where the Sun's magnetic field is zero.
mcq.explanation: L1 provides an uninterrupted, continuous line-of-sight to the Sun without Earth's eclipses, enabling continuous solar monitoring.

items.title: COP28 UAE Consensus & COP29 Baku Climate Summit: Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels
items.summary: The UNFCCC COP28 in Dubai adopted the historic 'UAE Consensus', calling on all nations to transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems to achieve net zero by 2050, followed by the COP29 summit in Baku focusing on the New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG) on climate finance.
items.crux: COP28 formally operationalized the Loss and Damage Fund hosted by the World Bank, and set global targets to triple renewable energy capacity and double energy efficiency rates by 2030.
takeaways: COP29 in Baku, Azerbaijan, was dubbed the 'Finance COP' to negotiate a new financial target replacing the previous $100 billion annual climate pledge.
India advocated for climate justice, differentiation under Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC), and affordable technology transfer.
India launched the Green Credits Initiative (GCI) on the sidelines of COP28 to incentivize voluntary environmental positive actions.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: COP28: UAE Consensus, Loss & Damage Fund; COP29: Baku, Azerbaijan (NCQG Climate Finance); India's Net Zero target: 2070.

mcq.question: The primary agenda and focus of the COP29 climate summit held in Baku, Azerbaijan was negotiating the:
options: Global Methane Pledge enforcement.
New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG) on climate finance.
Universal carbon border adjustment mechanism.
Global plastic ban treaty.
mcq.explanation: COP29 in Baku was dubbed the 'Finance COP', focused on establishing the New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG) to replace the $100 billion/year climate finance target.
